text: You are / KING [no badge or logo text]
scene: A round white-headed mascot with two dot eyes and a faint smile wears a tall gold cylindrical crown etched with triangular patterns, a red-and-gold robe over a blue tunic, a gold collar ending in two lion heads, and a belt buckle showing a winged-disc motif. Its raised open hand gestures toward the words and the other hand holds a purple sceptre with a gold finial. A hand-drawn black curved arrow starts above the words and arcs rightward toward the crown on a plain white background.
mechanism: A second-person role assignment: the sentence You are KING is pointed at a costumed figure, so the viewer is invited to occupy the top rank while the title promises every rank.
composition: Text occupies the left half and the costumed figure the right half, with the figure running off the bottom edge so the crown is the high point. The arrow bridges text to figure and acts as the reading path. White space around the words keeps the layout uncluttered, though the figure is close to the right edge.
typography: Three words in thin hand-lettered style, You are in black and KING in red, set on two lines at left. The letters are legible on the 320 sheet but the thin strokes weaken in the 160 render, where KING survives mainly through its red colour. The text names only one rank while the title says every rank, so it adds the king example and omits the Persian setting.
colors: White background with black lettering, one red accent on KING that echoes the red robe. The gold crown and sceptre give the only warm saturated area and separate cleanly from the white.
psychology: The figure's flat dot eyes and small smile give a neutral, welcoming look and the open palm reads as presenting. Gold crown, sceptre and lion collar are authority and status props rather than facial cues.
partnership: The title lists a rank-by-rank POV; the thumbnail picks the highest rank and uses the same you-address, so it complements rather than repeats. The unanswered question is what the lower ranks look like, and the king example shows the answer's top end.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red KING first, then the curved arrow, then the gold crown, then the robe and sceptre.
art: Clean cartoon rendering with outlined fills and gold shading on the crown, mixed with a plain blank mascot head that has no nose or ears. Lighting is flat and consistent and no cutout fringing is visible. The thin handwritten text style is the weakest element at phone size.
strength: The arrow plus the single red word make a fast one-glance proposition of being the king.
weakness: Nothing in the image says Persian or empire beyond a lion collar and a winged-disc buckle, so the setting is invisible at phone size.
bottleneck: Thin lettering plus a text-left, figure-right split means the 160 render depends on a red word and a small crown.
action: Hypothesis: add the word PERSIAN or a stack of three ranked figures beside KING and test whether the rank set is understood faster than with one figure.
counterexample: Seq 3 puts two named ranks side by side with bold facial detail, so the rank comparison is visible where this one shows only the top rank.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: COULD IT BE YOU? / $250K [no badge or logo text]
scene: A cartoon man with an oval head, orange-brown hair, wide round eyes and a gaping open mouth wears a blue T-shirt, jeans and white sneakers, and points a finger toward a red-roofed two-storey house with white siding and dormer windows. Above him a thought bubble holds a grey calculator, and a hanging price tag reading $250K with a red glow outline is attached to the roof. A black curved arrow runs from the headline down to the calculator, and the image sits in a 480x360 frame with black bars at top and bottom.
mechanism: A relatable affordability question: the pricing tag on the house and the calculator in the thought bubble make the money tension concrete, and the headline asks the viewer to place themselves in it.
composition: The man fills the left third and the house the right two-thirds, with the headline across the top and the price tag at the roofline near the centre. The pointing arm and the arrow create a diagonal loop between man, calculator, headline and tag. The picture is dense but the elements are separated by white space.
typography: Four black capitals words with YOU enlarged, plus a small $250K tag set at an angle. Black on white gives full contrast and COULD IT BE YOU? reads at 160x90, but the tag text becomes small. The headline repeats only the personal angle, while the $250K and 2026 context come from the tag and title.
colors: White background, red roof and tag outline as the saturated accent, blue shirt as a secondary mass. The red belongs to the house and its tag as a descriptive colour, and the cream house walls blend a bit with the white background.
psychology: The wide eyes and open mouth read as surprise or alarm, and the pointing hand directs attention to the house. The calculator thought bubble is a visible cue of budgeting.
partnership: The title asks who can afford a $250k house in 2026 and the thumbnail turns that into a personal COULD IT BE YOU? with the same price shown, so the price number is duplicated while the personal framing is added. The unanswered question is whether the viewer qualifies.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: bold YOU first, then the astonished man's face, then the price tag, then the house.
art: Flat vector cartoon with heavy outlines and a soft glow around the tag. Perspective on the house is slightly three-quarter and consistent, and the character is stylised in a recognisable sitcom-cartoon manner. The source is only 480x360 with black bars, so edges are slightly soft.
strength: One face, one house and one price tag give a quick, readable money proposition.
weakness: The low-resolution 480x360 source with letterbox bars softens the small $250K tag, the key number.
bottleneck: The price tag, the most specific item, is the smallest piece of text in the frame.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the $250K tag to roughly the height of the headline and test whether the number is found faster at phone size.
counterexample: Seq 22 uses a similar pointing cartoon man but makes the headline the main hero, while this one splits attention among man, bubble, tag and house.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: Rōnin / Shōgun [no badge or logo text]
scene: Two bust-length anime-style samurai face the viewer side by side on white. The left figure wears a conical straw hat, a mustard-yellow scarf over a blue robe and has a diagonal scar on his cheek, with two sword hilts wrapped in blue diamond-pattern cord crossed behind his shoulders. The right figure wears red lacquered armour and a helmet with large gold crescent horns, with a sword hilt visible at the right edge. Both have lowered brows, tight frowning mouths and direct gaze.
mechanism: A named two-rank comparison: each label sits over its figure, and the costume contrast between worn straw hat and gleaming horned helmet shows social distance in one frame.
composition: Mirrored left-right layout with the two labels aligned across the top and the faces at near-equal scale in the middle. Both figures run off the bottom edge, which gives a strong close-up. The hat brim and helmet horns echo each other as diagonals pointing inward.
typography: Two single-word labels, one per figure, in thin black rounded type at the top. Each word is about a fifth of the frame width and is still readable in the 160 render. The labels supply the rank words that the title only generalises as every rank.
colors: Pure white backdrop with high-saturation blue, mustard and red costumes. Blue/yellow on the left versus red/gold on the right colour-codes the two ranks, and the warm skin tones separate cleanly from the clothes.
psychology: Both faces show lowered brows and a flat frown with direct gaze, which reads as stern. The scar and the armour supply poverty-versus-power cues without text.
partnership: The title promises every samurai rank and the thumbnail shows two ranks with their names, so it complements the title by previewing the extremes. The unanswered question is what the ranks in between look like.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red-gold helmet first, then Shōgun, then the straw hat and Rōnin label, then the swords.
art: Polished cel-shaded illustration with consistent outlines and lighting. The head anatomy and costume details are coherent and nothing visible shows a rendering artefact, although the swords and cord patterns add fine detail that drops out at phone size.
strength: A clear two-card ranking comparison with labelled opposites and strong colour coding.
weakness: Both labels use thin rounded type that is lighter than the heavy illustration beneath it.
bottleneck: Equal-weight twin figures mean the eye has no single winner, so the scan path stalls between the two heads.
action: Hypothesis: make the Shōgun figure about 20 percent larger than Rōnin and test whether a clearer hero improves the first-glance read.
counterexample: Seq 1 shows only a single rank with a tiny mascot face, while this one gives two large faces and labelled opposites.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: NONE [no overlay text; in-scene signage only: SALE, SALE, SLUSHIE, Snackeroos, CHOCO BAR, VOLT]
scene: A convenience-store counter scene in cartoon style. A round bald-headed character in a navy cap and navy T-shirt smirks while tucking a dollar bill into his shirt pocket, with a hand resting on a bag of chips, a chocolate bar and a can on the counter. At the left edge a dark-haired man in a teal shirt looks on with wide eyes at a register, and at the right a woman with a hair bun covers her mouth laughing while a spiky-haired man in a striped sweater laughs and points, each holding a shopping basket. Shelves of snacks, ceiling lights, two SALE banners and a slushie machine fill the background.
mechanism: A tiny-purchase scene: the pocketed dollar, the snacks and the laughing onlookers imply a small daily spend that others mock, but no words anchor the story.
composition: The cap character stands in the centre with the counter forming a bottom band, the stranger frames the left edge and the laughing pair frames the right. The shelves create converging lines toward the centre. The frame is crowded, with many small package details competing around the focal figure.
typography: No overlay type is present, so the title carries the whole money message and the dollar bill is the only money cue. The only in-scene words are small SALE and brand signs that are unreadable at 160x90 and add nothing.
colors: Warm cream and orange interior with saturated primary colours on packaging and banners. The navy cap and shirt give the central figure good contrast against the beige shelves, while the busy product colours spread attention.
psychology: The central figure has a closed-mouth smirk and one raised brow, the pair at right have open laughing mouths, and the man at left has wide eyes. These reactions suggest mockery and surprise, though nothing signals warning or hope.
partnership: The title is about investing $5 a day and the thumbnail shows spending a dollar at a store, which is related but unspecific, and it never shows the $5, the investing or the outcome. The not-what-you-expected hint of the title has no visual counterpart.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the cap figure's face first, then the dollar bill in the pocket, then the laughing couple at right, then the counter snacks.
art: Detailed cartoon with consistent warm lighting and coherent perspective, rendered with fine shelf and packaging detail. Four human figures are drawn in two different styles, one bald mascot head and three realistic faces, which creates a style mix. Background complexity is high.
strength: The cast of four reacting people gives a clear social-reaction story around the cash.
weakness: With no text and a high-detail background, nothing in the frame says invest or five dollars.
bottleneck: The unreadable shop clutter at phone size leaves only faces and a green dollar as cues.
action: Hypothesis: add a large overlay such as $5 with an upward arrow over the counter and test it against the current text-free version.
counterexample: Seq 2 states its numeric hook in a big headline and price tag, which this scene lacks.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: NONE [no overlay text, logo or badge]
scene: A crudely drawn black-hooded figure with a brown face, rectangular black sunglasses and a flat horizontal mouth line holds out an arm whose open brown hand hovers palm-up beneath a floating yellow banana. A white drawstring hangs from the hood, and the background is plain white.
mechanism: A single odd image pairing: a cloaked, sunglassed figure offering a banana invites a joke-versus-finance curiosity, and the title supplies the crypto angle.
composition: The hooded figure takes the whole left half and runs off the top and left edges, while the banana floats at right of centre with the hand below it. The empty white area on the right gives the banana an isolated focal point.
typography: There is no overlay text, so the title alone carries the crypto topic. At 160x90 the banana and the dark hood still read, but nothing names the subject.
colors: High-contrast black, white and a single saturated yellow banana, with a brown skin tone as a muted secondary hue. The yellow is the only bright colour and pulls the eye to the hand.
psychology: The mask-like face has sunglasses and a flat mouth line, which reads as deadpan and gives no emotional cue. The hooded black clothing adds a mysterious, dealer-like atmosphere.
partnership: The title says Crypto Explained with Bananas, so the banana is a direct visual of the title's second half while the crypto half is missing. The thumbnail therefore adds attitude but not the topic.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow banana first, then the sunglassed face, then the offering hand, then the black hood.
art: Rough MS-Paint-style outline drawing with wobbly lines and flat fills, which looks deliberately low-effort. The scale of the face versus the hood and the arm is stylised rather than anatomically coherent, and the 1280x720 image shows slight blockiness around outlines.
strength: Very few elements and strong black-white-yellow contrast give an instant, memorable image.
weakness: Without text or a coin symbol, nothing visible communicates crypto or money.
bottleneck: The topic cue lives only in the title, so the thumbnail alone is a banana joke.
action: Hypothesis: place a coin or chart symbol in the hand opposite the banana and test whether the finance angle registers faster.
counterexample: Seq 9 from the same channel fills the frame with the word LIES, so that thumbnail names the topic while this one leaves it out.

text: THESE 7 LEG SIGNS / BLOCKED / ARTERIES AFTER 60 [no badge or logo text]
scene: The frame is split into a black text panel at left and a flat red panel at right. On the right a man with close-cropped grey hair and a grey beard wears navy scrubs with a stethoscope around his neck and points his index finger toward the left, with slightly raised brows and a half-open mouth. At lower left a white rounded-rectangle inset with a red glow outline shows a bare foot and ankle photographed side-on, with a wavy purple vein line running up the ankle.
mechanism: A symptom-checklist warning: a count of leg signs, a single huge BLOCKED word and an ankle close-up promise visible warning signs of artery disease, with a scrub-clad figure pointing at the evidence.
composition: Text stack and inset fill the left 55 percent in a vertical sequence, while the pointing figure fills the right edge. His finger and gaze create a leftward diagonal back to the text. The black/red split is blocky and tidy with little negative space.
typography: Three tiers: THESE 7 LEG SIGNS in white capitals, BLOCKED in very large yellow capitals, ARTERIES AFTER 60 in white on a red bar. BLOCKED and the red bar read clearly at 160x90 while the top line is smaller but still legible. The text restates the title's claim and does not add the word dangerously.
colors: Black and red panels with a yellow keyword and white caption text, a high-alarm palette. Red glow around the foot inset and the red bar reinforce the warning meaning, while the navy scrubs separate from the red background.
psychology: Slightly raised brows, a half-open mouth, a direct gaze and a pointing hand give an instructional, alerting presence, and the stethoscope plus scrubs cue medical authority. The age marker 60 targets older viewers.
partnership: The title and thumbnail share almost the same claim of seven leg warning signs of blocked arteries after 60, so the thumbnail mostly repeats it while the ankle inset adds a single example image. The unanswered question is what the seven signs are.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow BLOCKED first, then the red ARTERIES AFTER 60 bar, then the pointing man's face, then the ankle inset.
art: Photographic cutout of the man on a flat red backdrop with clean edges and consistent lighting, plus a white-background foot photo inset. Panel boundaries are hard and graphic, and no distortions are visible. Background complexity is low and the layout holds at phone size.
strength: BLOCKED in yellow on black has maximum legibility and a clear hierarchy beneath it.
weakness: The wavy purple line on the ankle is presented as an artery warning sign without any label, which could mislead.
bottleneck: A single unlabeled ankle photo carries the whole visual proof of seven different signs.
action: Hypothesis: replace the one ankle with a small numbered grid of two or three different leg findings, labelled neutrally, and test clarity against the single inset.
counterexample: Seq 10 uses a comparable warning layout but spells a concrete action in the headline instead of a symptom list.
medical_notes: The word BLOCKED over an unlabelled ankle photo with a purple vein line implies a diagnosable artery sign, and scrubs plus stethoscope appear with no printed credential.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: MODERN vs. ROMAN?
scene: A split-screen separated by a white lightning-bolt tear. On the left, in grey tones, a stick-figure man sits on a sofa with sweat drops flying, wipes his forehead with a cloth and has an open mouth, with wavy heat lines above while a floor-standing portable air-conditioner unit beside a window burns with orange flames, grey smoke and yellow sparks. On the right, in colour, a stick-figure man in a white toga with a laurel wreath reclines on a marble chaise with a hand propping his head, half-lidded eyes and a slight smile, while a smaller curly-haired attendant waves a peacock-feather fan in front of a waterfall wall and marble columns.
mechanism: A before-versus-now hot/cool contrast where the burning air conditioner and sweating figure on the left sets up the cooler luxury of the Roman side, answering the title's villa comparison visually.
composition: Even left-right split on a zigzag diagonal with the headline spanning the top. Both figures sit at about the same scale in the lower middle. The grey-to-colour switch makes the right half the winner and the fire at left is the strongest local accent.
typography: Three words in thick yellow capitals with a black outline across the full width, with vs. in a smaller size between. The text reads clearly at 160x90 and merely labels the two sides, while the title adds the heat angle that the headline lacks.
colors: Desaturated grey for the modern room against vivid cream, marble pink, aqua and peacock green for the Roman side. Yellow headline on both halves ties them together, and orange fire is the only warm accent on the grey side.
psychology: The left figure shows sweating, raised brows and an open mouth, a clear distress expression, while the right figure shows half-closed eyes and a small smile, a calm expression. The attendant with the fan adds a service-of-luxury cue.
partnership: The title asks why your house is hotter than a Roman villa, and the thumbnail turns that into MODERN vs. ROMAN? with an overheating room versus a cooled villa, so it complements by showing the heat. The answer is partly revealed since the Roman side looks cooler.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the burning air conditioner on the left, then the sweating figure, then the reclining Roman on the right.
art: Stick-figure doodle style with outlined shapes in a clean digital rendering. The left half is intentionally grey and the right is coloured, and both figures follow the same character design. Lighting and perspective are consistent and details such as fan feathers and flames remain readable at phone size.
strength: A clear split with a bold headline and an emotional contrast on both sides makes the comparison read in one glance.
weakness: The question mark and vs. headline offers little that the two pictures do not already show.
bottleneck: The right half's colour makes the Roman side look like the answer before the title's question is explored.
action: Hypothesis: add a thermometer value, such as 40 degrees on the left and a lower number on the right, and test whether a number sharpens the comparison.
counterexample: Seq 14 uses a single scene with one character, so it lacks the side-by-side contrast shown here.
hero_object: burning air conditioner and marble chaise
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: NONE [no overlay text; in-scene signage only: COFFEE HUB, B on cap]
scene: An office kitchenette in cartoon style. A figure with a large round beige head, a navy cap marked with a letter B, raised brows and a slightly open mouth, in a light-blue shirt and dark trousers, holds a paper coffee cup at a machine labelled COFFEE HUB. A bearded man in a green sweater with a lanyard badge leans in over his shoulder with a wide open-mouth smile, holding up a phone that shows a glowing green rising line chart with bars. Three more coworkers stand or walk in the blurred background beside windows with a city view.
mechanism: A pitch-at-the-coffee-machine scene: the glowing green chart on the colleague's phone suggests tips about money, while the cap figure's wary look sets up reluctance.
composition: The cap figure is at left-centre and the green-sweater man overlaps him on the right, so their faces and the phone form a triangle. The phone is bright and slightly right of centre as a secondary focal point. Background workers are softened by depth blur, keeping the foreground clear.
typography: There is no overlay text, so the Money Rules and POV wording stay in the title. The signage COFFEE HUB is too small to read at 160x90, and the chart on the phone is the only symbol.
colors: Warm window light and beige tones with a green sweater and green chart as the strongest accent. The glowing screen draws the eye, and the blue shirt and navy cap sit quietly against the beige.
psychology: The cap figure shows raised brows and a sideways mouth, a wary or surprised look, while the colleague has wide eyes and a big grin. Their body lean and the held-up phone create a pushy-pitch cue.
partnership: The title promises five money rules, and the thumbnail shows only a rising chart in an office chat, with no number or rule visible. It adds a social setting that the title does not state and says nothing about the five.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the glowing phone chart first, then the cap figure's face, then the grinning coworker, then the coffee machine.
art: Cartoon illustration with soft gradient lighting, depth-of-field blur and consistent perspective. The cap figure's oversized round head is drawn in a different, simpler style from the realistically drawn colleague, a visible style mix. A small four-point sparkle mark sits at the lower right corner of the frame.
strength: Clear two-person interaction with a bright phone screen gives a focal object.
weakness: No overlay words and a mild, generic office setting make the thumbnail look like many others of the same series.
bottleneck: At phone size the chart on the phone shrinks to a green smudge and the story is left to the faces.
action: Hypothesis: blow up the phone screen to show a single large number or green percentage and test whether the money cue reads at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 13 from the same channel adds a duffel bag of cash and a dealership sign, giving a more concrete money object than this scene's tiny chart.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: LIES
scene: A crudely drawn pink-faced figure with wild grey hair, thin-rimmed glasses, thick angled brows and a flat smirk line stands front-on in a black suit, light-blue shirt and yellow tie. Behind him, overlapping yellow bananas stacked in tilted rows fill both sides of the frame, and each banana carries the word LIES in black marker lettering.
mechanism: A repeated accusation: roughly thirty visible bananas stamped LIES surround a suited authority figure, so the Ponzi theme is shown as a wall of falsehood rather than a chart.
composition: The suited figure is centred and runs off the bottom edge, with the grey hair and suit forming a dark vertical shape against the yellow field. Banana rows tilt in opposite directions at left and right, giving a slight fan effect around him. The face is the single focal point and the pattern is the frame.
typography: One repeated word, LIES, in hand-drawn black capitals on every banana, which is dense in volume but identical in content. It stays legible as a texture at 160x90 and the unobstructed copies on the sides still read. It adds the accusation that the title only implies by the word Ponzi.
colors: Saturated banana yellow against black suit and grey hair gives very high contrast, and the yellow tie echoes the background. The pink face is the only warm-pink area, so it separates from the yellow. Yellow is used as a brand texture here rather than as an alarm signal.
psychology: The figure has lowered angled brows, glasses and a tilted flat mouth, which read as stern. The suit, tie and grey hair are authority-figure props and the LIES wall adds an accusatory cue.
partnership: The title says The Biggest Ponzi Scheme Explained with Bananas, and the thumbnail supplies the banana motif and the word LIES, so the key idea of deception is added beyond the title. The unanswered question is who the suit figure is meant to be.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the pink face with glasses first, then the nearest LIES bananas beside the head, then the yellow tie, then the wider banana pattern.
art: Deliberately rough digital doodle with uneven outlines, flat fills and some scribbled grey hair strokes. The face is an oversized pink rounded shape on a plain suit body, and nothing suggests a rendering error. The repeating pattern is busy but separated from the figure by contrast.
strength: A repeated LIES wall and a centred suited figure deliver the scam theme in under a second.
weakness: The pattern is so uniform that the eye gets no second point of interest after the face.
bottleneck: The word Ponzi and the scheme mechanics are absent, so only a general lying theme registers.
action: Hypothesis: replace one of the banana LIES with a coin or pyramid mark in the face's line of sight and test whether a single odd element adds a second read.
counterexample: Seq 5 from the same channel uses a nearly empty white background with one banana, so it is the opposite of this dense pattern.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: CHOKING ALONE? / DO THIS IN / THE FIRST / 20 SECONDS [no badge or logo text]
scene: On a black background an illustrated older man with receding grey hair and a lined face, wide pale eyes, tilted brows and a slightly open mouth grips his own throat with one hand. He wears a green-and-blue plaid shirt and takes up the right third of the frame, cropped at the shoulder. Four stacked text lines occupy the left two thirds.
mechanism: An emergency countdown: the grasping-the-throat pose names the situation and the 20-second figure sets a time limit, while the action itself stays hidden behind DO THIS.
composition: A left-text, right-face split with the headline stacked in four lines, the first line CHOKING ALONE? set smaller and the next three (DO THIS IN, THE FIRST, 20 SECONDS) set larger and of similar height, and the face at upper right. The hand at the throat sits low-right and leads the eye back toward the text. Black negative space between the blocks keeps the frame clear.
typography: Four lines: CHOKING ALONE? in yellow, DO THIS IN in yellow, THE FIRST in white, and 20 SECONDS in white on a red bar, nine words in total. Every line is large and legible at 160x90, with the 20 SECONDS bar the strongest block. The text nearly reproduces the title's wording and drops the after-60 detail.
colors: Black background carrying yellow, white and a red bar, a classic alert palette. The warm skin tone and the green plaid shirt stand out from black, and red is reserved for the time limit.
psychology: Wide eyes, tilted brows, an open mouth and a hand on the throat read as distress or alarm. The grey hair and lined face are visible signals of an older person, which cues the audience for the video.
partnership: Title and thumbnail share nearly the same wording about choking alone and the first 20 seconds, so the thumbnail mostly duplicates the title and adds the pose. The unanswered question is what to do, which both withhold.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow CHOKING ALONE? first, then the large white THE FIRST, then the red 20 SECONDS bar, then the man's face and throat.
art: Illustration in a semi-realistic painted style with consistent shading on the face and plaid shirt. The hand and fingers at the throat are anatomically coherent. The flat black background keeps the frame clean and the headline remains readable at phone size.
strength: A concrete scenario plus a short time limit gives a sharp, readable proposition in the text alone.
weakness: All four lines compete in size, so the 20 SECONDS bar and the question share equal weight.
bottleneck: The nine-word headline runs close to the title wording, leaving little unique information.
action: Hypothesis: trim the headline to CHOKING ALONE? and 20 SECONDS and test whether fewer words increase prominence of the face and hand.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses a similar warning palette but shows a symptom inset photo, while this one shows only the person in distress.
expression_label: wide eyes, open mouth, hand at throat
medical_notes: The packaging promises an urgent first-aid action within 20 seconds without showing or naming the method, so its safety depends on what the video teaches.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: RUB THIS OIL! / JOINTS FEEL 18 AGAIN! / SECRET OIL
scene: Left: two rounded panels show 3D-style knee joints, the first red-orange and pitted with a rough bone surface, the second smooth and pale with white cartilage caps. A yellow block arrow between them points right. Right: a glass bottle with a cork, golden liquid and a cream label reading SECRET OIL stands on a dark wooden surface against a dim blurred background.
mechanism: A before-and-after joint transformation claim attached to a single mystery product, where the red damaged joint becomes a smooth one beside the oil bottle.
composition: Three tiers: yellow-and-white headline at the top, a red caption bar below it, then the panel pair and bottle across the bottom. The bottle at right is a tall vertical counterweight to the wide panels, and the arrow drives the left-to-right reading to the bottle.
typography: Two bold lines in yellow and white capitals with 18 in yellow on a red bar, plus SECRET OIL on the label, nine words in total. The headline and bar read clearly at 160x90 while the label text is smaller but still readable. The text adds the 18 again promise that the title expresses as overnight aging relief.
colors: Dark brown background with warm golden oil, yellow headline and red caption bar. The inflamed red-orange left joint gives a danger colour against the cream healthy joint, and the yellow arrow links them.
psychology: No face is visible, so the cues are product and body imagery: red inflamed bone texture for pain, the pale smooth knee for relief and the secret label for exclusivity. The age number 18 is a visible rejuvenation cue.
partnership: The title says to rub this oil before bed and that it destroys joint pain, inflammation and aging overnight, while the thumbnail turns that into joints feeling 18 again, which escalates the claim with an age figure. The oil is unnamed in both.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow RUB THIS OIL! first, then the 18 on the red bar, then the red damaged knee, then the arrow to the smooth knee and the oil bottle.
art: Glossy 3D-render knees and a photo-real bottle composed with cinematic dark lighting. The pitted red joint texture is more graphic than anatomical, and the two panels look like clean inset boxes. The mixture of render and photographic bottle is visible, but no concrete artefact is evident.
strength: A strong before/after pair with an arrow and an obvious product bottle makes the claim readable instantly.
